blueprints.subject: maths
blueprints.title: Large numbers to 100,000
blueprints.objective: Reads, compares and uses whole numbers up to 100,000 within age-appropriate contexts.
blueprints.teach: Read and compare whole numbers by place value from ten-thousands to ones. Decompose a number to show the value of each digit.
blueprints.workedExample: In 74,215, what value does the digit 7 represent? The 7 is in the ten-thousands place, so its value is 70,000.

guidedTry.prompt: In 74,215, what value does the digit 7 represent?
guidedTry.hintLevel1: Name the place of the leftmost digit.
guidedTry.hintLevel2: The 7 is in the ten-thousands place, so its value is 70,000.

masteryTransfer.prompt: A town recorded 96,405 visitors and another recorded 96,450. Which is larger?

blueprints.reviewPrompt: Later, try a fresh large numbers to 100,000 task and explain the clue, rule or evidence you used.
blueprints.narrationText: Read and compare whole numbers by place value from ten-thousands to ones. Decompose a number to show the value of each digit.

blueprints.subject: maths
blueprints.title: Estimation and reasonableness
blueprints.objective: Estimates before calculating and uses the estimate to detect unreasonable answers.
blueprints.teach: Estimate by rounding to a useful place before exact calculation. Use the estimate to reject answers that are far too large or too small.
blueprints.workedExample: Estimate 398 + 205 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred. 398 rounds to 400 and 205 rounds to 200, so the estimate is 600.

guidedTry.prompt: Estimate 398 + 205 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
guidedTry.hintLevel1: Round each addend to the nearest hundred.
guidedTry.hintLevel2: 398 rounds to 400 and 205 rounds to 200, so the estimate is 600.

blueprints.reviewPrompt: Later, try a fresh estimation and reasonableness task and explain the clue, rule or evidence you used.
blueprints.narrationText: Estimate by rounding to a useful place before exact calculation. Use the estimate to reject answers that are far too large or too small.

blueprints.title: Factors and multiples

blueprints.workedExample: Which number is a factor of 24? 24 ÷ 6 = 4 with no remainder, so 6 is a factor of 24.

blueprints.narrationText: A factor divides a number exactly. A multiple is made by multiplying that number by a whole number.

blueprints.title: Inference with evidence
blueprints.objective: Makes an inference and cites relevant textual details that support it.
blueprints.teach: An inference combines a reasonable idea with evidence from the text. Choose the inference only when a specific detail supports it.

blueprints.subject: english
blueprints.title: Main idea and summary
blueprints.objective: Identifies central ideas and produces a concise summary without copying every detail.
blueprints.teach: A good summary states the central idea and only the most important supporting information. It does not copy every small detail.
blueprints.workedExample: Text: “The class tested three paper-bridge designs. After comparing how much weight each held, they strengthened the best design.” Which is the best summary? The best summary gives the central action—testing designs—and the important result—improving the strongest one.

guidedTry.prompt: Text: “The class tested three paper-bridge designs. After comparing how much weight each held, they strengthened the best design.” Which is the best summary?
guidedTry.hintLevel1: Keep the main action and result, not every detail.
guidedTry.hintLevel2: The best summary gives the central action—testing designs—and the important result—improving the strongest one.

blueprints.reviewPrompt: Later, try a fresh main idea and summary task and explain the clue, rule or evidence you used.
blueprints.narrationText: A good summary states the central idea and only the most important supporting information. It does not copy every small detail.
